 1          Plaintiff Wade Benton, in his capacity as Sellers’ Representative (“Plaintiff”) and
 2   Defendant CiVi Biopharma Holdings, Inc. (“CiVi”) and collectively with CiVi and Plaintiff, “the
 3   Parties”), hereby submit this Joint Case Management Statement pursuant to the Court’s Order,
 4   Dkt. No. 102.
 5          I.       JURISDICTION AND SERVICE
 6          This is a breach of contract action between parties that are citizens of different states or of
 7   foreign states, in which the sum in controversy exceeds $75,000. The Court has subject matter
 8   jurisdiction over this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a).
 9          II.      FACTUAL BACKGROUND
10          Plaintiff’s Statement
11          Plaintiff Wade Benton—the Sellers’ Representative under a 2018 Stock Purchase
12   Agreement (“SPA”)—alleges that CiVi breached its core obligation to pay a $2,000,000 Base
13   Purchase Price within 60 days after FDA approval of the first NDA for an Eicos-developed
14   iloprost product, and refuses to provide assurances regarding future contractual Milestone
15   Payments based on sales of FDA-approved iloprost products. The FDA approved Aurlumyn
16   (iloprost IV) for severe frostbite on February 13, 2024, triggering payment by April 13, 2024, yet
17   CiVi has not paid despite repeated written demands and the SPA’s plain terms. Plaintiff also seeks
18   indemnification for Losses (including attorneys’ fees) under the SPA’s indemnity provisions.
19          Plaintiff further alleges that, after defaulting, CiVi transferred Aurlumyn rights to
20   Defendant BTG via an Asset Purchase Agreement (“APA”) in or around October 2024, and
21   that BTG intentionally interfered with the SPA by facilitating a transaction that stripped CiVi of
22   key assets and obscured sales reporting, making CiVi’s performance more difficult or impossible
23   and perpetuating the nonpayment. Plaintiff seeks damages for interference as well as rescission of
24   the SPA, returning the approved NDA to Benton, if CiVi’s material breach is not cured.
25   The declaratory judgment claim seeks confirmation that the Base Purchase Price was due April
26   13, 2024, that future Milestones must be paid as achieved, and that CiVi (and any
27   successor/assignee as shown by the evidence) remains responsible for those obligations.
28

 1          Plaintiff looks forward to proceeding with the case, including by seeking summary
 2   judgment on his breach of contract and declaratory judgment claims, now that the Motions to
 3   Dismiss are resolved.
 4          Defendants’ Statement
 5          In 2018, Plaintiff and the other selling shareholders of Eicos Sciences, Inc. (“Eicos”)
 6   made a deal (the SPA) that provided for contingent consideration if, and only if, CiVi achieved
 7   certain milestones, including FDA approval, for a product developed for one of three specific
 8   medical indications. Even with Plaintiff’s assistance and CiVi’s investment of significant
 9   resources, including on multiple clinical trials, CiVi never obtained FDA approval for any such
10   product and thus the contingent milestone payment never came due. Plaintiff then, years after the
11   fact, sought a new deal with different terms, demanding to “amend” the SPA to eviscerate its
12   limitation to products developed for three specified medical indications and to expand it to cover
13   any medical indication. However, the selling shareholders provided no consideration for any such
14   new deal, nor were they signatories to the purported amendment.
15          III.    DISPUTED LEGAL ISSUES
16          The key legal issues disputed by the Parties are described in Defendants’ Motions to
17   Dismiss the Second Amended Complaint, filed February 2, 2026, which the Court decided in Dkt.
18   No. 103. The Parties reserve the right to identify additional disputed legal issues in the future.
19          IV.     MOTIONS
20          There are no motions currently pending.
21          V.      AMENDMENT OF PLEADINGS
22          The Parties are engaged in settlement discussions, the possibility of a settlement
23   conference before a magistrate or mediation as necessary to resolve those discussions. The Parties
24   propose that a further case management conference be set after the current settlement discussions
25   are concluded, but in no event later than December 1, 2026, at which time the Parties can address
26   deadlines, including those for amendment of pleadings.
27          VI.     EVIDENCE PRESERVATION
28          Plaintiff’s Statement

10          VIII. DISCOVERY
11          The Parties are engaged in settlement discussions, the possibility of a settlement
12   conference before a magistrate or mediation as necessary to resolve those discussions. The Parties
13   propose that a further case management conference be set after the current settlement discussions
14   are concluded, but in no event later than December 1, 2026, at which time the Parties can address
15   deadlines, including those for a Rule 26(f) conference and other discovery.
16          IX.     CLASS ACTION
17          This case is not a class action.
18          X.      RELATED CASES

21          Plaintiff seeks damages, indemnification against losses (including attorneys’ fees) and
22   rescission of the SPA.
